summary:
Turn 76 linked the confirmed executor timeout to an actual recovery start, closing the last gap in the liveness picture.

What was observed locally. A harness blocks row 1 at an instance whose record has no commands, starts the real executor goroutine, waits for the timeout path (the enqueue arrives after about 12.9 seconds), and then hands that enqueued entry to the recovery entry as the run loop would. The result is a started recovery: the record is in preparing state with one self reply in its bookkeeping and 34 bytes emitted on the wire (the Prepare broadcast). So the timeout path does not merely signal a blocked instance — it leads to a live recovery attempt, which is the continuation the dead accept-rejection path (C7) depends on.

Product. A second artifact on the same unit (unit-C8-timeout-enqueues-blocked-instance): a new plan and harness whose prerequisite is the confirmed enqueue event and whose property asserts preparing == true on the recovery-started event, with instance identity correlating the two, the existing timeout-trigger binding and grounding, and the honest note that the harness calls the recovery entry itself rather than letting the run loop consume the channel (the loop's own consumption is out of scope). No requirement, predicate or observation from the first C8 scenario is altered.

Frontier. The liveness question is now covered end to end within the harnesses: an unexecutable row is enqueued after the grace period and the enqueued instance enters recovery. The eleven claim families, the two paused candidates, the structurally stuck scope issue and the remaining unread items are unchanged, and no requirement, premise or earlier observation was weakened.
